title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 09 (Full-Book Board Simulator II)
subject: english-10

questions.question: Identify the underlined word: 'The horse ran *fast*.' 'Fast' is an:
questions.explanation: 'Fast' answers 'How did the horse run?' modifying the verb 'ran', which makes it an Adverb of Manner.

questions.question: Choose the transitional device indicating ADDITION of points: 'Reading books expands your worldview; ___, it sharpens analytical reasoning.'
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces supplementary reinforcing evidence, functioning as an additive transitional device.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The old merchant is blind ___ the faults of his son.'
questions.explanation: 'Blind in/of' one eye refers to physical sight deficiency, while 'blind to' denotes figurative unawareness or refusal to acknowledge faults.

questions.question: What is the central moral theme of the poem 'Try Again' by W.E. Hickson?

options.A: Resilience, tenacity, and persistent effort in the face of initial failure
options.B: The inevitability of defeat in life
options.C: The beauty of nature and seasons

questions.explanation: 'Try Again' preaches that failure is not a disgrace but a stepping stone; consistent perseverance will eventually conquer all obstacles.

questions.question: Ali said, "I can solve this puzzle easily." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: Ali said that he can solve that puzzle easily.
options.B: Ali said that he could solve that puzzle easily.
options.C: Ali said that he could solve this puzzle easily.
options.D: Ali told that he would solve that puzzle easily.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'can' shifts to 'could', and proximal demonstrative adjective 'this' shifts to distal 'that'.

questions.question: Select the passive voice: 'The principal gave the boy a scholarship.' (Focusing on the recipient)

options.A: The boy was given a scholarship by the principal.
options.B: A scholarship had been given to the boy by the principal.
options.C: The boy was giving a scholarship by the principal.
options.D: A scholarship was gave by the principal to the boy.

questions.explanation: When a sentence has both an indirect object ('the boy') and direct object ('a scholarship'), either may be the subject; here 'The boy was given a scholarship by the principal' correctly promotes the indirect object.

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'I will be preparing for my final examinations this time next week.'
questions.explanation: 'will be preparing' represents an ongoing action at a specific time in the future, which is the Future Continuous tense.

questions.question: In which sentence is the word ending in '-ing' a GERUND?

options.A: Gardening requires immense patience and care.
options.B: The gardening tools were left in the shed.
options.C: He was gardening when the thunderstorm began.
options.D: Look at the man gardening under the sun.

questions.explanation: In option A, 'Gardening' is the subject of the sentence, acting as a noun (Gerund). In B, it acts as a noun adjunct/modifier; in C and D, it is part of a verb or a participle.

questions.question: Identify the underlined clause: 'He failed *because he did not take his studies seriously*.'
questions.explanation: 'because he did not take his studies seriously' explains the cause of his failure, constituting an Adverb Clause of Reason.

questions.question: Identify the modal: 'The lights are on; he *must* be at home.'
questions.explanation: 'Must' based on evidential proof ('The lights are on') indicates epistemic certainty and strong logical deduction.

questions.question: Identify the underlined word: 'He is a *fast* runner.' 'Fast' is an:
questions.explanation: Here 'fast' directly modifies the noun 'runner', functioning as an Adjective.

questions.question: Identify the subordinating conjunction in: 'You will succeed provided that you stay focused on your goals.'
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' is a complex subordinating conjunction introducing a conditional clause.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'Karachi is ___ Manchester of Pakistan.'
questions.explanation: When a proper noun ('Manchester') is used as a common noun for comparison/analogy, it takes the definite article 'the'.

questions.question: In Dr. Silvia Hartmann's poem 'Peace', what does the wind represent in its stormy state?

options.A: A monster of raw destructive fury and chaos

questions.explanation: In its raging state, the wind is depicted as a roaring monster crushing and smashing all creations of mankind.

questions.question: The commander said to the soldiers, "Halt!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The commander requested the soldiers to halt.
options.B: The commander commanded the soldiers to halt.
options.C: The commander told the soldiers for halting.
options.D: The commander asked the soldiers that they halt.

questions.explanation: Military and authoritative orders require reporting verbs like 'commanded' or 'ordered' followed by an infinitive ('to halt').
